
A lesson in CoAuthor is a set of short slides. Most slides ask you to do something before they tell you anything. This guide shows you what to expect.

## Guess first, then find out

Many slides follow three steps:

1. **Predict.** The slide asks a question before it teaches the idea. You make your best guess.
2. **Observe.** A simulation or a picture shows what really happens. Watch it, and compare it with your guess.
3. **Explain.** The slide asks you why it happened. Now the idea has a reason behind it.

Guessing first is not a test. Scientists work this way too. When your guess is wrong, you notice the surprise, and you remember the idea better.

> [!TIP]
> Do not skip the guess, even when you are not sure. A quick, honest guess helps you more than a careful copy of the answer.

## Moving through a slide

- Press **Next** to see the next part of a slide. Some slides show their points one at a time.
- Press **Back** to read an earlier part again.
- On a computer, the <kbd>Right</kbd> and <kbd>Left</kbd> arrow keys do the same.
- Simulations have their own buttons and sliders. Try them. You cannot break anything.

## When you get an answer wrong

Wrong answers are fine here. In a lesson you lose no marks and no points. The question shows you why the answer was not right, and the lesson carries on so you can use the idea straight away.

![A lesson question after a wrong guess. The chosen answer is marked Not this one, the right answer is marked, and a note explains why the guess was not right.](media/lesson-wrong-answer.png "A wrong guess in a lesson. You see the right answer and a short reason, and you lose nothing.")

Here is a small question to try. Choose an answer and press **Check**.

```coauthor-try
{
  "id": "guide-first-lesson-q1",
  "type": "mcq-single@2",
  "stem": { "en": "A heavy stone and a light pebble are dropped from the same height, where there is no air. Which reaches the ground first?" },
  "options": [
    { "id": "a", "text": { "en": "The heavy stone" }, "isCorrect": false },
    { "id": "b", "text": { "en": "The light pebble" }, "isCorrect": false },
    { "id": "c", "text": { "en": "Both reach the ground together" }, "isCorrect": true }
  ],
  "explanation": { "en": "Without air, everything falls with the same acceleration. In normal air, a feather falls slowly only because the air pushes back on it." }
}
```

## Hints

Many questions have hints. The first hint gives a small push. Later hints say more. Use a hint when you are stuck, not before you have tried.

## Stars and XP

You earn XP for finishing lesson steps and for right answers. XP counts how much you practise. It is not a mark. Your progress is saved after every step, so you can stop and come back later.
